passage_evidence.literal_claim: The title concerns parameter inference. The first two opening paragraphs motivate spatial field variety and describe a thresholded random-input model that predicts distributions, rather than exact next-field locations.
passage_evidence.support: PLACE-GP defines a distribution over fixed functions and the threshold rule; PLACE-INFERENCE derives threshold and scale from occupied and inactive means. Later PLACE-DATA and PLACE-TOPOLOGY supply the shape/hole checks. The opening retains 'may' for possible cell patterns and attributes the model to the paper rather than treating it as measured hidden input.
passage_evidence.qualification: The word 'strongest' is an assessment of why further shape tests help distinguish models, not an asserted numerical ranking. It is supported by the later spherical-field alternative and separation of fitted versus additional quantities. No correctness repair needed.

passage_evidence.literal_claim: Track crossings lead to counts; field and gap lengths separate threshold and scale; the sampled map stays fixed through movement.
passage_evidence.support: PLACE-KAC-RICE derives the crossing density and finite-track endpoint correction. PLACE-INFERENCE divides active/inactive fractions by crossing density and explicitly inverts their means. PLACE-GP takes expectations over possible maps or cells. Thus spatial coordinate and time are kept distinct.
passage_evidence.qualification: The overview summarizes crossing counts; the first relevant heading and complete calculation explicitly retain the active-left-endpoint correction. It does not discard that convention or promise an exact finite-sample ratio rule.

passage_evidence.literal_claim: High peaks give a way to explain the distribution of sizes, which a mean length alone does not specify.
passage_evidence.support: The preceding PLACE-INFERENCE determines means and warns that means do not determine distributions. PLACE-RARE-PEAKS takes a high-threshold limit, derives excess height and local radius, and PLACE-SIZE-LAW changes radius into length, area and volume.
passage_evidence.qualification: 'Unusually high' in the opening and the explicit approximation in the next paragraph prevent the title from claiming an exact finite-threshold law. The body keeps its regularity and asymptotic assumptions.

passage_evidence.literal_claim: A local parabola links height to radius and dimensional size. Slices and boundary slopes check further spatial structure. The slope law and high-threshold size law have distinct validity ranges.
passage_evidence.support: PLACE-RARE-PEAKS displays the parabolic expansion and radius formula. PLACE-SLICES explains Gaussian restriction and sampling cautions. PLACE-SLOPES derives the slope-weighted exact Rayleigh boundary law without a high threshold and its folded independent width check uses the parabolic approximation.
passage_evidence.qualification: The opening explicitly calls the parabolic form approximate and distinguishes the exact boundary-slope derivation under the smooth stationary Gaussian assumptions. It does not transfer exactness to the width check.

passage_evidence.literal_claim: The continuation carries z, q, sigma, a, d and the rectified firing rule from the first spatial chapter.
passage_evidence.support: The normalized variance-one input, threshold and gain were explicitly defined in PLACE-GP. The reminder gives all symbols needed before the Hessian calculation, including the positive-part notation. Units remain spatial distance, normalized input, and rate gain.
passage_evidence.qualification: No conflict with memory theta or diffusion D is introduced.

passage_evidence.literal_claim: Size and count agreement leaves holes and arrangement open, and agreement with the spatial model does not by itself establish a circuit mechanism.
passage_evidence.support: PLACE-TOPOLOGY distinguishes connected-component counts from holes/tunnels and derives Euler characteristic. PLACE-WIRING gives one random-summation mechanism and explicitly lists other possibilities and unmeasured weights/input.
passage_evidence.qualification: The opening asks what agreement would imply; it does not claim that every map has holes or that a unique wiring pattern follows.

passage_evidence.literal_claim: Joint component and hole counts predict a threshold-dependent statistic with boundary terms; data processing/fitting must be separated from further tests; random weighted inputs supply a possible Gaussian mechanism under conditions.
passage_evidence.support: PLACE-TOPOLOGY supplies signed densities and box boundary coefficients. PLACE-DATA identifies fitted parameters, processing and added tests. PLACE-WIRING states independent zero-mean weights, a central-limit condition, no dominant input, and separate spatial assumptions.
passage_evidence.qualification: 'One way' and 'could' keep sufficiency distinct from identified biological causation. Boundary terms are preserved rather than silently replaced by a large-box approximation.

passage_evidence.literal_claim: Map randomness is still spatial; q, sigma, a and d retain their meanings, and dimension d differs from memory diffusion D.
